    Cross-universe thin-path retractions for bound sources #

    This file is the quotient analogue of CrossUniverseThinPathRetraction. The free quiver is thin, but some of its paths may vanish in a linear Hom-ideal quotient. Normalization is therefore stated after multiplying the quotient path itself. A killed path imposes no impossible equation such as 0 = 1, while the same coefficient table still proves a Hom-bifunctor retraction of the bound source.

            HomBifunctorRetraction D

            Pathwise coefficient equations extend to a cross-universe Hom-bifunctor retraction of the bound quotient source.

            Instances For

              Quotients which identify parallel paths #

              The free quiver need not itself be thin. For a commutative diamond, for example, there are two parallel free paths although their images in the bound quotient agree. The following variant records exactly that weaker condition. The rest of the path-basis argument is unchanged: freeness is used upstairs to extend from paths by linearity, while uniqueness is needed only after passing to the quotient.

                  HomBifunctorRetraction D

                  Pathwise coefficient equations extend to a cross-universe Hom-bifunctor retraction when parallel paths agree in the bound quotient.

                  Instances For

                    Finite endpoint compiler #

                    For concrete bound quivers it is more convenient to prescribe one coefficient for every ordered pair of vertex occurrences and check covariance only for arrows. The next structure iterates those finite equations along paths and produces the path-indexed data above.
